summary: Franklin County, NY tower built in 1927 for the Adirondack-Florida School; still standing on private land and closed to the public, per Wikipedia.

access.note: On private land and closed to the public, per Wikipedia; no recent visit report found

events.note: Built by Conservation Department Forest Ranger Albert Tebeau for the Adirondack-Florida School

evidence.supports: in the Adirondack Mountains of New York
evidence.quote: mountain located in Adirondack Mountains of New York

evidence.supports: northeast of Paul Smiths, Franklin County
evidence.quote: It is located in the northeast of the hamlet of Paul Smiths in Franklin County
Meenahga Mountain is a 2,087-foot-tall (636 m) mountain
The mountain is the site of a 73-foot-tall (22 m) Aermotor LS40 fire lookout tower.

evidence.supports: built 1927 by Ranger Tebeau for the school
evidence.quote: In 1927, Conservation Department Forest Ranger Albert Tebeau built a 73-foot-tall (22 m) Aermotor LS40 tower on the mountain for the Adirondack-Florida School.

evidence.supports: school used it most; state fire use under DEC agreement
evidence.quote: The tower was mostly used for the school, but was used as a fire observation station in times of high fire danger through an agreement with the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

evidence.supports: still stands; private land; closed to the public
evidence.quote: The tower still remains but is on private land and is closed to the public.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia spells it Meenahga Mountain; the Forest Fire Lookout Association index and the AARCH list use Meenagha, the record's spelling. Kept as Meenagha.

sources.title: Fire Towers in New York State

notes_for_editor: Build year, design and private status rest on Wikipedia, which cites the NYSFFLA searchable list; we could not open that list. The Adirondack Forum post is a visitor's remark, cited only as unverified. No staffing record, fire record, recent photo or condition report found. No corrections proposed; the record name is kept, though Wikipedia uses Meenahga.
